sources_considered.why: Version-pinned contemporaneous primary evaluation demonstrates bounded autonomous task completion.
Version-pinned primary evaluation includes repeated trials and concrete failure analysis.
The unversioned page includes later revisions; the original version is used instead.
read_page returned only a redirect notice; the paper supplies the substantive record.

evidence_items.explanation: The evaluated agents completed bounded tasks autonomously, with approximately even odds at a difficulty corresponding to 50 minutes of human work. This contradicts 'no proof', while a 50% success rate plainly does not establish dependable general autonomy.

The study's repeated evaluations document failures when agents cannot cheaply verify progress, alongside other planning and recovery failures. These findings support the practical concern about dependable autonomous work, but not an absolute inability to act autonomously.

unresolved_gaps: Neither study establishes reliability across the full range of ordinary work.
The speaker supplies no threshold separating limited autonomy from the autonomy he considers meaningful.
Releasing methods and observing repeated successes is not equivalent to independent replication of every result.
